Author: Saurabh Shyam Shamshery
Bench: Saurabh Shyam Shamshery
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 76
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Cancellation Application No. - 415 of 2022
Applicant :- Chhatthu

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And Another Counsel for Applicant :- Lal Dhari Rajbhar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Jawahar Lal Maurya Hon'ble Saurabh Shyam Shamshery,J.

A coordinate Bench of this Court has granted bail to accused Jaishraj @ Deshraj, who is facing trial in Case Crime No. 287 of 2021 under Sections 452, 504, 506, 354-Kha, 376 I.P.C. and 3/4 of POCSO Act, Police Station- Shahganj, District- Jaunpur, after considering opposition of learned A.G.A. for State and learned counsel for informant.
The present application is filed for cancellation of bail on behalf of applicant/informant.

Sri L.D. Rajbhar, learned counsel for applicant submits that coordinate Bench has not considered the first information contents, statements of victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.,
that they were intact and consistent against applicant that he has committed offence referred above and in terms of Section 439 (2) Cr.P.C., this Court has power to cancel the bail of accused and learned counsel has placed reliance upon a judgment of Supreme Court in X (Minor) Vs. State of Jharkhand and another, 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 194.

sentences.text:
S/Sri Rishi Chaddha, learned A.G.A. for State and Jawahar Lal Maurya, learned counsel for opposite party/accused have opposed above submissions that arguments raised by learned counsel for applicant are akin to review the order which is barred under the provisions of Section 362 Cr.P.C.
and for that remedy lies to challenge the said order before Supreme Court.
I have considered rival submissions of parties and perused record.

It is considered opinion of this Court that arguments referred above by learned counsel for applicant are akin to review the bail order passed by coordinate Bench which is specifically barred under Section 362 Cr.P.C.

There is no doubt that this Court has power to cancel the bail, however, it will only when conditions prescribed in bail order are violated or a fraud is played by applicant/accused in extraordinary circumstances.
However, it is not a case in present case as all materials were available before coordinate Bench and there was an objection of learned counsel for informant also.
Therefore, I do not find any reason that on the basis of above submissions, prayer to cancel the bail granted to accused can be allowed.
In view of above, this bail cancellation application is rejected.
However, applicant/informant has liberty to challenge the order granting bail to accused, before Supreme Court, if so advised.

Order Date :- 20.4.2023 Nirmal Sinha  Chhatthu vs State Of U.P. And Another on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34599161/
